per_claim.item: M1 — dim g₂ = 14, g₂ = Der(𝕆), and su(3) branching 14 = 8 ⊕ 3 ⊕ 3̄
per_claim.corrected_claim: CONFIRMED. g₂ (Lie algebra of G₂, the automorphism group of the octonions) is 14-dimensional (rank 2: 12 roots + 2 Cartan) and equals Der(𝕆). Under its maximal-rank su(3) subalgebra the adjoint 14 branches as 8 ⊕ 3 ⊕ 3̄ via the Z₃-graded decomposition (natural module + its dual; 8+3+3=14). Standard Lie theory; Baez 'The Octonions' Bull. AMS 39 (2002) for Der(𝕆), Draper arXiv:1704.07819 for the Z₃-grading. Caveat (opus): no single fetched page printed the literal '8+3+3̄' string — the branching is forced by maximal-rank embedding + Z₃-grading + dimension count, not byte-verified from a primary branching table (Slansky 1981 / Yamatsu arXiv:1511.08771 would close this).

per_claim.item: M2 — exactly four Hopf fibrations with Hopf invariant one (Adams 1960)
per_claim.corrected_claim: CONFIRMED. Exactly four Hopf fibrations have Hopf invariant one: S⁰↪S¹→S¹, S¹↪S³→S², S³↪S⁷→S⁴, S⁷↪S¹⁵→S⁸ (n=1,2,4,8); octonionic total S¹⁵, base S⁸, fiber S⁷, 15=8+7. Adams, 'On the non-existence of elements of Hopf invariant one', Annals of Mathematics 72 (1960) 20–104. Precision note (sonnet+opus): some formulations emphasize n=2,4,8 as the non-trivial cases, treating n=1 (real S⁰↪S¹→S¹) as degenerate; the four-fibration listing is nonetheless standard (Wikipedia, nLab). Opus flags the page range 20–104 as matching universal citation but not independently byte-verified.

per_claim.item: M3 — Hurwitz's theorem: normed division algebras ℝ/ℂ/ℍ/𝕆 (dims 1,2,4,8; imaginaries 0,1,3,7); commutativity/associativity ladder
per_claim.corrected_claim: CONFIRMED. The only normed (composition) division algebras over ℝ are ℝ/ℂ/ℍ/𝕆, dims 1,2,4,8 = 2ⁿ; imaginary-unit counts 0,1,3,7 = 2ⁿ−1. The Mersenne label is arithmetically correct (1,3,7 = 2¹−1,2²−1,2³−1; 3 and 7 are Mersenne primes, 0 and 1 are degenerate). ℂ commutative; ℍ non-commutative (associative); 𝕆 non-commutative AND non-associative (but alternative). Hurwitz 1898; equivalently the composition-algebra form. All parts verified.

CONFIRMED (integer-trivial, self-checking). The Cayley-Dickson tower doubles 1→2→4→8; graded increments for the ℂ/ℍ/𝕆 part are 2 + (4−2) + (8−4) = 2+2+4 = 8 — the NESTED telescoping sum. This is correctly distinguished from the PARALLEL sum 2+4+8 = 14 (= dim g₂, reached by a separate algebraic route). The two routes to 8 and 14 must not be conflated; the framework's F405 distinction is mathematically sound.

per_claim.item: M5 — sedenions 𝕊 (dim 16) are NOT a division algebra (zero divisors, lose composition norm)
per_claim.corrected_claim: CONFIRMED as stated. Sedenions (dim 16, Cayley-Dickson double of 𝕆) are not a division algebra: they contain zero divisors (explicit example (e₃+e₁₀)(e₆−e₁₅)=0) and lose the multiplicative-norm/composition property (failure of alternativity for n≥4 in the C-D tower); they remain power-associative and flexible. The M5 claim itself does not depend on any specific zero-divisor count.

The specific count is NOT a single clean number — this is the most important MPM-discipline finding of the pass, and all three tiers converge on it. Three non-interchangeable counts appear in the literature: 84 'sets'/diagonal lines (Wikipedia; de Marrais), 168 primitive unit zero-divisors (de Marrais arXiv:math/0011260), and 42 Assessor pairs (same paper); Moreno (arXiv:q-alg/9710013) separately showed the norm-one zero-divisor space is homeomorphic to compact G₂. Haiku marked the enumeration unverified/low-confidence; sonnet enumerated all three counts and required convention-specific attestation; opus tied '84' to de Marrais (84 sets/lines, 42 Assessors) and to F410, recommending the framework tighten '84 zero-divisors' to '84 zero-divisor sets/diagonal lines, 42 Assessors'. Any framework citation of a specific count must pin the exact paper AND counting convention per MPM.

per_claim.item: M6 — Klein four V₄ = Z₂×Z₂ and Q₈/{±1} ≅ V₄
per_claim.corrected_claim: CONFIRMED. V₄ ≅ Z₂×Z₂ by definition. Q₈ = {±1,±i,±j,±k} has center {1,−1} (order 2); the quotient Q₈/{±1} has order 4 with every non-identity element of order 2 (i²=j²=k²=−1 ≡ 1 in the quotient), hence ≅ V₄ (the unique non-cyclic order-4 group). Standard finite-group theory.
